doc: Root view: the session Store drives routing, hot partitions drive lobby/board/settings, and the cold cache drives history and card details.
Cold callback cache: fetched history pages and open card details.
Handle Kanban client-local operations; returns false for operations that should go to the server.
Dropping the private user partition (logout, revoked access) clears cached private cold data.
After a board update, refetch only open card details whose hot detail-rev moved forward.
Card detail panel fed by the cold cache; shows cached content revision next to the hot detail-rev so staleness is visible.
Small text input keeping its draft in Respo component state and submitting one domain operation.
Personal history from cold pages. The private hot partition only announces history-rev, so new events show as a count until the user loads them.
What a pending request id will update: the history list (append or replace) or one open card detail.
Cold data the browser has fetched. Only open card details are kept; history pages accumulate until history-rev announces newer events.
Apply a reply only if its request id is still pending; closed panels, superseded requests and older content revisions are ignored.
Open card details whose hot detail-rev moved past the cached content revision; only these are refetched, unused content is never downloaded.
Forget older requests for the same target so their late replies are ignored.
Hot board state shared by every authorized subscriber of the board partition.
Bounded lobby summary of one board.
Hot card summary. The description lives in cold storage; detail-rev tells clients when a cached detail is stale.
Cold card content. rev matches Card :detail-rev after the same committed operation.
Cold writes derived purely from one committed domain operation.
Cold data kept outside the hot Db and the Reel: append-only per-user history and versioned card details. Swap for a database-backed store without touching partition sync.
One Kanban column ordered by a numeric rank field, so reordering changes leaves instead of list positions.
Cold, append-only personal operation history entry.
Newest-first page of personal history. next-cursor is an exclusive index into the append-only log, stable under appends.
Business operations of the Kanban demo. The acting user always comes from the session; payloads only name target ids and values.
Public hot partition: board briefs and online user names keyed by user id.
Private hot partition of one user. history-rev only announces that cold history changed; events are fetched by query.
Personal hot preferences synchronized to every connection of the same user.
Validate persisted cold storage before it is used for queries.
Validate one untrusted Kanban operation payload before it reaches the reducer.
Cold history and card details. They are written by committed operations and read only through queries.
Append cold history and card details derived from one committed operation.
Per-user bound of the in-process cold history log used by this template.
File holding cold history and card details, separate from the hot database snapshot.
Project one partition with the current cold store (only history-rev is read from it).
Answer one cold read using the session identity; history is always the caller's own.

Partitions whose projection may change after one operation, computed from the database before the operation (so log-out still dirties the old user). Only live partitions are re-projected; route changes only alter subscriptions.
Bounded public lobby: board briefs and online user names. Passwords and per-session data never enter it.
Project one partition from hot state. The user partition only carries history-rev from cold storage, never the events themselves.
Server-side authorization: only signed-in sessions subscribe, only to their own user partition, and to the board they currently route to. Logging out drops every partition.
Append history and replace card details. Per-user history is bounded; trimming shifts cursors, so clients re-read the first page after history-rev changes.
Pure Kanban reducer. Anonymous sessions and invalid targets leave the database unchanged.
Columns ordered by rank.
Read cold card content only while the hot card exists; the returned rev lets clients drop stale responses.
Cards of one column ordered by rank.
Deterministic database with one signed-in session (1) and one anonymous session (2) for reducer tests.
Newest-first page ending before an exclusive cursor into the append-only log; page size is clamped to 1..50.
Derive cold writes from a committed operation by comparing the touched board before and after; rejected or no-op operations produce no history.
Move a card to the end of another column by changing two leaves: column-id and rank.
Rank after the current maximum; appending never rewrites sibling ranks.
Swap ranks with the neighbor above or below inside the same column; only two rank leaves change.
Board, missing-board, open-detail resources, user view and empty resources for SSR checks of the Kanban views.
Called after a partition snapshot or patch is published, e.g. to refetch stale cold content.
Feature structs and enums that ws-edn must restore by name inside partition views and query replies.
Handle feature client-local operations; return false to send the operation to the server.
Called when the server revokes a partition; clear private caches tied to it.

Side effects after a committed operation, such as appending cold data, before partitions are published.
Answer one cold read. Identity must come from the session, never from query parameters.
Persist feature-owned state next to the hot database snapshot.
Project one partition. A partition is a visibility boundary: include only data every subscriber may see.
Server-side authorization: the partitions this session may subscribe to.
Per-connection session Store (route, session messages, login state).
Pure domain reducer used by the Reel.

A path-aware failure produced while decoding untrusted or legacy persisted database data.
The nominal hot application database used by reducers and partition projections. Cold history and card details live outside it.

A persisted session message.
Why an untrusted WebSocket value could not become a typed message envelope.
Identity of one synchronization partition. A partition is a visibility boundary: everything inside is visible to all its subscribers.
Typed projection of one partition; :missing marks a deleted or unknown target.
Cold read requests. Identity always comes from the server session, never from query parameters.
Typed cold read results, distinguishing missing content from denied access.
Concrete payload for removing one session message.
The domain route stored for one session; target names the routed entity such as a board id.

Current nominal ws-edn client, retained across browser recovery events.
Client-side reason for rejecting a revisioned patch before requesting a full snapshot.

Whether a fast coalesced server sync callback is pending.
Encoded latest single-delta patch of one partition lineage and revision.
Partition sync counters. diffs counts partition diff computations, independent of subscriber count; sends count per-connection fan-out.
Atomic server decision. Snapshot variants carry statistics and an optional budget reason but never partial changes.

Apply the acknowledgement a client sends after applying the given partition state's revision; used by ack-partition! and regression tests.

Commit one domain operation to hot state, append its cold effects, then mark only the partitions it can affect before publication.
